title: The King's Son and the Ifrit's Mistress

keywords: the king's son and the ifrit's mistress
full_text:
Prince Faris, son of the King of Khorasan, was hunting in the rugged mountain passes when he heard the sounds of sorrowful weeping echoing from an iron-barred cave in the cliffside. Approaching the bars, he discovered an innocent princess of India who had been abducted and imprisoned there by an evil Ifrit who dwelt upon the volcanic crags.

The maiden wept: 'Fly, brave prince, before the demon returns! None can withstand his fiery wrath!'

Prince Faris replied with steady valor: 'A true knight does not abandon the helpless in the hour of peril.'

Observing that the cave was locked with a talismanic bronze padlock inscribed with ancient riddles, Faris used his knowledge of ancient languages to decipher the inscription:
'The lock that iron cannot break
Shall open for the brave who speak:
What force is greater than the flame,
Yet bears no sword and boasts no name?'

Faris answered aloud: 'Truth and pure justice!'

The bronze lock snapped open instantly! Faris helped the maiden onto his stallion just as the ground shook and the monstrous Ifrit descended from the clouds, brandishing a flaming brand!

Faris drew his father’s ancestral blade, reflecting the afternoon sunlight into the demon’s eyes, and struck the talismanic crystal upon the monster’s breastplate. The crystal shattered, and the Ifrit dissolved into a plume of harmless smoke that was carried away by the mountain wind.

Faris escorted the princess safely back to her father’s court in India, establishing an enduring alliance of peace between the two kingdoms founded on courage and chivalric honor.
moral: Courage to defend the vulnerable breaks the power of the fiercest oppressive forces.
